blockers: None fatal, but three latent type-system traps WILL ship broken if the D1 snippet is implemented naively; all three were reproduced with the repo's tsc 7.0.2 and each has a verified fix (see amendments 2-4): (a) storing `errorStatus: {[K in keyof Errors]?: number}` on the descriptor interface makes Errors invariant and breaks assignability of every specific operation to the Any-op top type, which breaks feature()'s constraint and createApplication; (b) `Port.adapter()` returning a generic `BoundPortAdapter<Ops>` makes Ops invariant on PortDescriptor and breaks `ports: [NoteStorage]` and adapter arrays; (c) constraining feature()/port() collections as `Ops extends Record<string, AnyUnboundOperation>` contextually poisons omitted optional fields with generic defaults — a command/port-op with no `errors` infers Errors = ErrorSchemaMap (error type becomes `{code: string; details: unknown}`) instead of never, silently destroying error-narrowing everywhere and breaking the design's own `if (!saved.ok) return saved;` idiom.

Scanner: D1's rename makes every feature invisible to the compiler unless packages/compiler/src/scanner.ts:25-32 gains the short names — descriptorCalls only maps defineFeature/defineCommand/... spellings; `calledName` for `import { feature }` returns "feature" which misses the map, so zero drafts are collected.

Scanner: single-file features break `featureSegment` (scanner.ts:156-161) — verified: `src/features/notes.ts` yields segment "notes.ts" and `src/features/notes.test.ts` yields "notes.test.ts", so feature-id-by-segment mapping, test-to-feature association (scanner.ts:846-851), and all architecture diagnostics key on wrong segments; and the public-contract rule (scanner.ts:337, `basename(target) === "contract"`) flags every cross-feature import as `architecture.private-cross-feature-import` once contract.ts is deleted — D1 must redefine what the public contract is (the feature file itself) or drop/rewrite that rule.
amendments: Adopt the verified descriptor split (full working signatures preserved at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-WebstormProjects-agentix/5edd8286-fd74-4ada-940b-9ef875d62011/scratchpad/verified-d1-type-signatures.ts): `command()` returns id-less `UnboundOperation<Kind, Input, Output, Errors, Effects, Emits>`; `feature: <const Id extends string, const Ops extends Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>>(id: Id, def: {operations: Ops & ValidOperations<Ops>}) => FeatureDescriptor<Id, BindOperations<Id, Ops>>` where `BindOperations<FeatureId, Ops> = { readonly [K in keyof Ops & string]: Ops[K] extends UnboundOperation<infer Kind, infer I, infer O, infer Err, infer Eff, infer Em> ? BoundOperation<`${FeatureId}.${K}`, Kind, I, O, Err, Eff, Em> : never }`. Same pattern for ports: `BoundPortOperations<PortId, Ops>` deriving `${PortId}.${K}`. Verified: `notes.operations.create.id` is the literal type "notes.create".

Keep `execute` as METHOD syntax on descriptor interfaces and keep the conditional guard in every handler-mapped type (`EffectContext<Effects> = { [N in keyof Effects]: Effects[N] extends AnyPortOperation ? EffectHandler<Effects[N]> : never }`, same for EventEmitter/PortImplementation). Both are load-bearing: removing the guard (plain `EffectHandler<Effects[N]>`) makes specific descriptors non-assignable to the Any-op top type under strictFunctionTypes — reproduced, then fixed by restoring the guard. The current descriptors.ts already uses this pattern; do not 'simplify' it in the rewrite.

Store `http` on descriptors as variance-neutral `HttpMetadata` (`errorStatus?: Readonly<Record<string, number>>`); enforce error-code keys only in the authoring parameter type `AuthoredHttp<Errors> = {...; errorStatus?: { readonly [Code in keyof Errors]?: number }}` on command()/query(). Verified: typo'd `errorStatus: {TYPO_CODE: 400}` is rejected at the call site while descriptor assignability stays intact.

`Port.adapter(impl)` must return a NON-generic `BoundPortAdapter` (operations typed opaquely as `Readonly<Record<string, (input: never) => MaybePromise<Outcome<unknown, unknown>>>>`); the impl parameter stays `PortImplementation<Ops>` so adapter callbacks still infer (verified: `save: async (note) => ...` infers note: Note type).

Declare collection type params as `const Ops extends Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>` plus a `Ops & ValidPortOps<Ops>` / `Ops & ValidOperations<Ops>` parameter intersection (`ValidX<Ops> = { [K in keyof Ops]: Ops[K] extends TheShape ? Ops[K] : TheShape }`). Verified this preserves omitted-field generic defaults (errors -> never) AND rejects junk properties at the call site; the naive `Record<string, AnyUnboundOperation>` constraint poisons defaults (probe4) and `any`-slotted constraints don't help (probe5).

Application typing: `Application<Ops>` with Ops UNconstrained — `ApplicationOperations<Features> = UnionToIntersection<OperationsRecordOf<Features[number]>>` where `OperationsRecordOf<F> = F extends FeatureDescriptor<infer Id, infer Ops> ? { [K in keyof Ops & string as `${Id}.${K}`]: Ops[K] } : never` cannot satisfy a Record constraint at the declaration site (TS2344, reproduced). Use guarded helpers `OpInput<Op> = Op extends AnyBoundOperation ? Infer<Op["input"]> : never` (same for output/errors) and `dispatch<Id extends keyof Ops & string>(id: Id, {input: OpInput<Ops[Id]>, principal}): Promise<DispatchResult<OpOutput<Ops[Id]>, OpError<Ops[Id]>>>`. Verified: exact ids autocomplete/typecheck, "notes.remove" and wrong input shapes and unbranded id strings are compile errors, error unions narrow to `{code: "NOTE_EXISTS", details: {id: NoteId}}`, and multi-feature apps merge correctly.

Schema: `s.object()` must return an `ObjectSchema<S>` exposing `readonly shape: S` (design's `Note.shape.title` — today object() returns bare `Schema<ObjectOutput<S>>`, schema.ts:239-241), and `s.string()` needs the `{min, max}` options bag (today it takes no arguments, schema.ts:140). Both verified as stubs in the probe.

Scanner (packages/compiler/src/scanner.ts) — still statically analyzable, with these concrete changes: (1) add short names to descriptorCalls (line 25); (2) Draft handling (lines 558-587): feature/port ids move from an `id:` property to argument 0 (string literal) with the def object at argument 1; event() becomes positional (id, version, payload) with no object literal at all, so the `metadata.static-object-required` shape check must become per-kind; (3) operations extraction: replace top-level command/query variable drafts with iteration of the feature's `operations` object literal using the EXISTING port-operations mechanism (lines 647-691) — propertyName key + unwrap(initializer) must be a command()/query() CallExpression, derive id `${featureId}.${key}`, and register the property-name symbol in an operationBySymbol map plus a text fallback, exactly like portOperationBySymbol/portOperationByText (this same dual mechanism already resolves references through definePort's mapped return type today, so `notes.operations.create` in tests and `NoteStorage.operations.save` in effects keep resolving); (4) port op kind comes from the callee name (`port.write` — calledName already returns "write" for property-access callees, line 216-218) instead of a literal `kind:` prop (replace lines 659-663); (5) diagnose-and-mark-unresolved for computed keys, spreads, and non-call property values in operations/ports objects (the diagnostic pattern already exists); (6) extract the new `http` sub-object into IndexedOperation via existing objectExpression/stringLiteral/numberLiteral helpers; (7) replace the IndexedFeature.contract extraction (lines 902-921) with exportedNames of the feature file itself.

Architecture rules: strip extensions in featureSegment (and normalize `.test`/`.spec`/`.agent-test` suffixes for test association), and redefine the public-contract rule for contract-less single-file features — recommend: importing `src/features/<x>.ts` from another feature IS the public contract import; anything under a `src/features/<x>/` subdirectory (if it exists) is private. Also decide where `dependencies` are declared now that defineFeatureContract is gone (keep an optional `dependencies` field on feature(), or derive edges from imports); scanner's undeclared/unused-dependency diagnostics (lines 419-444) need whichever source is chosen.

Design doc D1 should state the static-authoring contract explicitly (it is what keeps the compiler lockstep honest): operation/port maps must be inline object literals with identifier or string-literal keys whose values are direct command()/query()/port.X() calls (as-/satisfies-wrapped allowed — unwrap() handles those) or identifier references to same-file consts; anything else gets a diagnostic and lands in `unresolved`.
